newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa sees chance for 97 cargo profit.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees chance for 97 cargo profit.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday it saw a chance for its cargo unit to end the year with a profit after recording an operating profit after the first four months of the year.
"Lufthansa Cargo at the end of April was operating in the black," Lufthansa Chairman Juergen Weber said in answer to a question at the airline's annual general meeting.
"The trend at the moment is positive," Weber said. "When nothing bad happens, and the trend continues, then we could end the year with a profit."
He noted that the fourth quarter would be decisive in determining how the year ends for the airline's cargo unit.

Lufthansa's cargo unit, hurt by falling prices in the air freight market, reported a loss on ordinary activities of 59.8 million marks in 1996 despite a three percent rise in sales to 3.43 billion marks.
In the 1997 first quarter, the unit reported a 11 percent rise in sales to 872 million marks.
